semantic_contract: All four objects must be inside the box, down on its bottom, each lying with its length along the box's long direction.

Each object's front end must point toward world -X, the robot's own left and the side of the table where the left arm is mounted, with its back end toward world +X. This is what the instruction means by front sides facing left; the direction is fixed in the world and does not change with the camera view.

The front end is the car's nose, the electric toothbrush's brush-head end, the hammer's head end and the shoe's toe. The back end is the car's rear, the bottom end of the toothbrush handle, the free end of the hammer's handle and the shoe's heel.
The box must stay upright with its long direction running along world X.
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.

review_notes: Source: pack_objects_into_box_random.py is the base module with only the concrete class renamed (line 237); every method span hashes equal to the base's.

END IDENTIFICATION (2026-11-14 read-only mesh probe with pxr from the RoboDojo runtime's USD libraries, no Kit, simulation or GPU; no Kit, simulation or GPU): each object.usdz opened with Usd.Stage.Open, every Mesh's points read into the default prim's frame (extents equal the metadata aligned_bbox for every model), then the cross-section extent at each end of the evaluator's checked axis, a 12-bin extent profile and side/top silhouettes. Controls: the base config's car 0/6/7, electric_toothbrush 0-3, hammer 0-4 and shoe 0-7 reproduce the base functional_axis_review (checked end = rear, handle bottom, handle free end, heel).

Variant models: car 1-5 (side silhouette: low hood at the other end, then cabin, and trunk, tall SUV rear, fastback or rear wing at the checked end; car 1 and 5 along local Y); electric_toothbrush 4-6 (narrow brush head and neck at the other end, wide cylindrical handle at the checked end); hammer 6 and 7 (claw hammers) and 8 (a mallet): wide head at the other end, handle at the checked end; shoe 8-17 (low toe box at the other end, heel counter at the checked end). Every checked axis points at the back end, so the base bullets are reused verbatim; functional_axis_review lists each model.
hammer/00008 is a mallet (rectangular head) rather than a claw hammer; 'the hammer's head end' and 'the free end of the hammer's handle' still name its ends.

evaluator_dependencies add the layout-0 models' object.usdz (car, toothbrush, hammer, shoe), as sort_nesting_dolls_by_size binds its dolls' meshes: the public end definitions rest on mesh geometry, so a model change fails preflight.
No clutter in this variant; its generalization is object models and scene materials only.

EVALUATION CADENCE (unchanged from the base record): run_reward is registered once at reset and reward_manager.step is called once per native action after its physics steps drain; a check stage latches when all its conjuncts hold at one native-action boundary (reward_manager.py:357-494), and get_reward returns 1.0 only when every check list is empty (reward_manager.py:527-587).
